public_rationale: The antecedent holds. The WSJ reported in July 2026, and again in October, that OpenAI plans about $750B of compute spending through 2030, though that window is longer than his 3.5 years. The forecast is that OpenAI will need either revenue of hundreds of billions a year 'very soon' or to raise $500B or more 'over the next few years'. By 2026-10-28 neither arm had happened, and neither had failed. OpenAI's revenue was about $12.4B in the first half of 2026. Its largest round, $122B, closed before the post. No decisive event settled it early: no $500B raise, no $200B revenue year, and no cut to the compute plan. The window runs to about February 2030, so the forecast is not due.
limitations: 'Very soon' and 'next few years' are undated; the outer bound is my reading.
A 'need' claim is hard to falsify if OpenAI defers or cuts spending.
The reported projection's window (through 2030) differs from his 3.5 years.

our_interpretation: Antecedent: OpenAI has a projection of about $750B in compute spending. The reports say 'through 2030', while he says 3.5 years. I treat the antecedent as met if the projection is publicly reported, and note the window mismatch.

The two funding arms keep his separate timing words. The revenue arm is 'very soon': annual revenue of at least $200B (the plain reading of 'hundreds of billions'). He gave no date, and no date is imposed here beyond 'well within' the 3.5-year spending window. The financing arm is 'over the next few years': cumulative new equity plus debt of $500B or more raised by OpenAI, read as no later than t…

The claim is about necessity ('will need to'). It is supported if OpenAI keeps spending on the projected path and funds it through one of the two arms. It is contradicted if OpenAI spends on that path while revenue stays well below $200B a year and cumulative raises stay below $500B.
The clause about hyperscalers having trouble raising money is context and not scored.
criteria.support_condition: OpenAI keeps the ~$750B compute plan, and either reaches $200B+ in annual revenue soon or raises $500B+ in cumulative equity and debt by early 2030.
criteria.contradiction_condition: OpenAI carries out spending on the ~$750B path through the window while its annual revenue stays well under $200B and cumulative new financing stays under $500B.
